# Fluent API Guide

This guide demonstrates common fluent patterns across the question types.

## General rules

- set_* methods overwrite/replace existing values
- add_* methods append to list-like attributes

## SingleChoice examples

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe import Q, Text
sc = (
    Q.SingleChoice(name="SC/Basic", questiontext=Text("<p>Pick one</p>"))
    .set_choice_correct("A")
    .set_choices_wrong("B")
)
sc
```

Note:
- SingleChoice.add_choice_correct is guarded and will raise if a correct answer already exists. For advanced scenarios (e.g., partial-credit experiments), use low-level add_answer or set_answers. Validation still enforces exactly one correct with fraction=100.

## MultiChoice examples

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe import Q, Text
mc1 = (
    Q.MultiChoice(
        name="Capitals/TH",
        questiontext=Text("<p>Capital of Thailand?</p>")
    )
    .set_choices_correct("Bangkok")  # 1 item -> 100
)
```

Note:
- MultiChoice.add_choice_correct follows the colorful/safe contract:
  - If no correct exists, it adds 100.
  - If corrects are uniform and sum to 100, it recalculates a new uniform fraction and snaps to the nearest allowed Moodle fraction (e.g., 33.33333 for 1/3). If it can't snap (e.g., 100/11), it raises and recommends using set_answers.
  - If existing corrects are non-uniform or don't sum to 100, it raises and recommends using set_answers.

## Multiple-answer with two correct answers (50/50) and two wrong answers

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe import Q, Text
mc2 = (
    Q.MultiChoice(
        name="Capitals/EU",
        questiontext=Text("<p>Pick EU capitals</p>")
    )
    .set_choices_correct("Paris", "Berlin")  # -> 50 each
    .set_choices_wrong("Madrid", "Zurich", fraction=0.0)
)
mc2
```

## Non-uniform fractions: use low-level set_answers

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe import Q, Text, Answer
mc3 = Q.MultiChoice(name="Math/Primes", questiontext=Text("<p>Pick primes</p>"))
mc3.set_answers(
    Answer.Text(text="2", fraction=60),
    Answer.Text(text="3", fraction=40),
    Answer.Text(text="4", fraction=0),
)
mc3
```

## TrueFalse examples

```{python}
#| echo: true
# pulls from examples/truefalse.py pattern, but run inline for Quarto
from questionsafe import Q, Quiz
q = (
    Q.TrueFalse(
        name="Logic/DeMorgan",
        questiontext="True or False: Not(A and B) == (Not A) or (Not B)"
    )
    .set_correct_if_true()
)
Quiz([q]).to_xml()[:200]
```

### Notes

- Re-invoking set_* rebuilds and overwrites previous choices and feedback unless provided again.
- For templating overrides (XML/HTML), pass templates_dir to render_xml/render_html.

## Safe API index

You can list the "safe" (validation-proof) methods programmatically:

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe import Q
from questionsafe.base import list_safe_apis
list_safe_apis(Q.MultiChoice)
```

```{python}
#| echo: true
list_safe_apis(Q.SingleChoice)
```

```{python}
#| echo: true
list_safe_apis(Q.TrueFalse)
```

Tip: In many IDEs, safe methods are also prefixed with "[SAFE]" in the tooltip since their docstrings are annotated.

## API summary (selected)

- Common to all questions: set_name, set_questiontext/ask, set_feedback_general, set_defaultgrade, set_tags/add_tag, set_idnumber
- Hints and penalties: add_hint, set_hints (penalty can be "auto"), set_penalty
- Combined feedback: set_combined_feedback, set_feedback_correct/partiallycorrect/incorrect
- MultiChoice: set_numbering, set_shuffle, set_single, set_choice_correct, set_choices_wrong, set_answers
- TrueFalse: set_choice_correct, set_choice_wrong
- ShortAnswer: set_usecase, set_answers, add_answer
- Numerical: set_answers, set_units/add_units
- Essay: various setters for response and attachments
